name: Remi Sigurdsson-Sigurdsson
role: Clothing and fashion vendor, specializing in geneware-compatible garments and custom aug-fit tailoring
location: The Alban Souk, Bronzeline, near Halsted and Division
description:
Remi Sigurdsson-Sigurdsson is medium height with her Ghanaian mother's rich dark skin and her Armenian father's long, expressive hands that she uses constantly when she talks — sketching shapes in the air, measuring invisible distances, framing imaginary necklines. Her geneware includes a set of bioluminescent tracery lines running from her temples down her jaw and throat, a deep blue-violet that she originally got for professional display purposes (showing clients how light interacts with their own potential geneware) and has now had so long she forgets other people can see them. Her hair is geneware-modified to grow in precise architectural shapes she redesigns quarterly; currently a structured asymmetric sweep with the texture of woven textile rather than hair. She dresses to demonstrate, always — in things she has made or modified, things that show what she can do.

Remi Sigurdsson-Sigurdsson's stall in the Alban Souk has expanded twice since she set it up seven years ago and now occupies a corner unit with a small fitting alcove curtained off from the main market floor. She makes most of what she sells — adaptive fabrics that accommodate tail geneware, spine-following cuts for aug users with dorsal hardware, clothes that move with retractable claws rather than tearing on them. She is opinionated about aesthetics in the specific way of someone who thinks about it constantly and seriously, and will talk about garment theory for as long as you'll allow, which most of her regulars have stopped allowing because they have places to be. She is cheerfully pushy about what will suit a person and usually right, which is what keeps people coming back.

core_fears: Her work becoming obsolete — that fashion will shift away from handmade and personal in a direction she can't follow
Her younger sister, who is Tier 1 and refusing help, getting swallowed by Irkalla
core_desires: Recognition — not fame exactly, but for her work to be taken seriously as craft, not just market goods
To design a complete geneware-adaptive collection significant enough that a Tier 3 boutique would carry it
coping_mechanisms: Channeling anxiety into elaborate new design projects
Social busyness — being around people in the Souk functions as mood regulation
blind_spots: Her professional confidence bleeds into overconfidence in her ability to manage people's problems — she often takes on other people's crises as design problems to solve, which doesn't work
Underestimates how much the two geneware clinics that refer clients to her control her market position
psychology.secret: She has been secretly making and donating geneware-compatible clothing to a Tier 1 mutual aid network in Irkalla for two years — clothing designed specifically for people whose geneware has grown out of the cheap stuff they could afford and now tears or tangles in standard garments. She keeps it secret because she's afraid people will think she's performing charity. She's also afraid she'll get too attached to the work there and lose focus on building her own business.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Fast and visual; describes everything in terms of texture, fit, and color; Twi and Armenian endearments mixed into everyday speech; market shorthand with vendor peers
speech_patterns.cadence: Enthusiastic and slightly too fast, with sudden focused slowdowns when she's assessing something seriously
verbal_tics: Touching the fabric she's wearing as punctuation
'You see what I mean?' (whether or not you see what she means)
example_lines: 'No, but look — the problem is the shoulder seam, you've been wearing the wrong shoulder seam for your whole augmentation profile and it shows in how you hold yourself, I can see it from here. Sit.'
'The Souk has been strange this week. Strange like — not the usual strange, different strange. You've been around, you know?'

story_hooks: Her sister has pawned something at Constant's shop on the Gray Zone — something of their mother's — and word has reached Sabine through the vendor network. She needs someone to help her recover it quietly before the standard resale period expires.

A Helix Biosystems rep has approached her about designing a line of 'clinically certified geneware-compatible garments' under a Helix brand license — which would mean real money and distribution, but also corporate oversight of her designs and a non-compete that would kill her independent work. She's been agonizing over it for two weeks.
narrative_function: Social hub and neighborhood gossip network node, equipment and clothing source for characters needing aug-compatible gear, potential quest giver for problems involving the Souk community.
augmentations: Geneware: bioluminescent facial tracery (blue-violet), architecturally-structured hair modification. Cyberware: measurement implant in both hands (precise dimensional scanning for fitting purposes, outputs to a visual overlay). No other augmentations.
daily_life: Alban Souk opens at 08:00; she's there at 07:00 setting up displays. Afternoons are peak fitting hours. Evenings she works on commissions in the back of the stall. Takes Tuesdays off to source fabric from Ironvein industrial suppliers.
affiliation: Independent; Alban Souk vendors collective; informal professional relationship with two Bronzeline geneware clinics who refer aug clients to her for fitting

decision_rules: Make things well — shortcuts in craft compound into regret
Help people in the Souk community before outside obligations
Never let a corporate offer be the only offer on the table before deciding
escalation_ladder: Redirect with questions and topic reframing
Direct statement of objection with immediate pivot to alternatives
Cease interaction entirely and become very publicly busy
Loud, precise, surgical public disagreement — she is very good at this and uses it sparingly

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Immediately warm and assessing — she's reading your augmentation profile and silhouette simultaneously
interpersonal_modes.friends: Bossy and affectionate in equal measure; will fix your collar without asking permission

stress_responses.low: Talks faster; bioluminescent tracery brightens slightly
stress_responses.medium: Gets very focused and quiet on whatever her hands are doing — sewing, measuring, folding
stress_responses.high: Exits the situation to find fabric and works until she can think again

contradictions: Craves professional recognition but hides her most meaningful work from public view
Pushes people to present themselves authentically while maintaining a very curated professional persona herself
habits: Touches the hem of whatever she's wearing when thinking
Always has a measuring tape somewhere on her body
Leaves worn fabric scraps at the Souk's central ELF shrine — considers it an offering of material transformed into something better
breaking_points: Her work being called decorative or trivial by someone who benefits from it
Her sister being in serious danger while refusing Sabine's help

timeline.event: Age 17 — began selling altered secondhand clothes from a bag in the Alban Souk
Secured permanent stall; began specializing in aug-compatible tailoring after a gap in the market became obvious
First geneware clinic referral relationship established; stall expanded to corner unit
Began anonymous donations to Irkalla mutual aid network
Helix Biosystems licensing offer received; currently unresolved

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly Southeast Asian (62.6%, primarily Vietnamese/Thai/Indonesian ancestry) with significant East Asian heritage (23.5%), Northern European (7.0%), North African (4.3%), and Hispanic/Latin American (2.6%) ancestry—a complex global blend reflected in warm-toned golden-brown skin with subtle olive undertones and refined facial structure
physical_description.build: Lean and graceful, with defined shoulders from years of precise hand work and pattern-cutting. Long-limbed with the kind of posture that comes from constantly observing fabric drape on bodies.
physical_description.hair_color: Deep black with structural iridescence from geneware modification
physical_description.hair_style: Asymmetric architectural sweep, left side layered short and angled upward, right side longer; texture resembles woven textile or structured mesh rather than organic hair
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-brown with subtle olive and amber undertones, luminous depth from the interplay of dominant Southeast Asian ancestry (62.6%) with East Asian (23.5%) and North African (4.3%) components creating rich, complex skin radiance
physical_description.complexion: Clear and well-maintained, with precise grooming and refined bone structure reflecting the ancestral blend. Bioluminescent tracery lines run symmetrically from temples down cheekbones to jawline and throat—deep blue-violet, faintly glowing in low light, creating a pattern resembling circuit paths or kintsugi lines
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent geneware tracery on both temples, framing the eyes and running downward in delicate branching patterns
Continuous luminescent lines along both sides of the jawline and extending down the throat, glowing blue-violet
Fine measurement scars on both palms from cyberware implant integration, nearly invisible but palpable
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent facial and throat tracery (active, gently glowing in ambient light). Hands show minor scarring from measurement implant cyberware but augmentations are functionally invisible—the implants output to a neural visual overlay only visible to her. Hair structure is clearly geneware-modified rather than natural, with an almost textile quality.
physical_description.posture_movement: Constantly in motion with hands—gesturing, sketching shapes in air, measuring invisible distances, framing proposed garment lines on clients' bodies. Stands with weight slightly forward, ready to move, to adjust, to demonstrate. Eyes track fabric and body movement with professional intensity. Speech is animated and accompanied by hand choreography.
physical_description.clothing_style: Always self-designed and modified pieces showcasing her own work. Currently wearing a reversible asymmetric jacket in adaptive polymer weave (blue-black on one side, deep purple on the other) with integrated measurement nodes at the shoulders and wrists. Fitted turtleneck in geneware-compatible textile that bridges the luminescent lines on her throat, emphasizing rather than hiding them. Custom-tailored trousers with reinforced seams at the calves for her own work-station movement. All pieces show visible stitch-work and seams as design features. Jewelry is minimal—measurement implants themselves serve as wrist adornments. Tier 3–4 aesthetic: independent vendor wealth, carefully invested in demonstration pieces and tools rather than status brands.
